planting.note: Plant during winter dormancy in very acidic, well-drained soil; Pearl River is an LSU AgCenter rabbiteye release bred for Louisiana's mild-winter, high-rainfall growing conditions and needs a second rabbiteye variety such as Climax or Brightwell nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Amend soil to pH 4.5-5.0 with peat or sulfur before planting; Pearl River is a rabbiteye blueberry released by the LSU AgCenter specifically for Gulf South dooryard and commercial plantings, selected for consistent production under Louisiana's mild winters and low-to-moderate chill hours. The medium-sized, light blue berries ripen mid-season and have a firm texture and mild, sweet flavor well suited to fresh eating and freezing. Plants are vigorous and moderately disease-tolerant, though they benefit from mulching with pine bark or pine straw to keep the shallow root system cool and moist. Not self-fruitful, so plant with at least one other rabbiteye cultivar within 50 feet for reliable cross-pollination and full-sized fruit. Prune out the oldest, least productive canes each winter to keep the bush renewing itself.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Blueberry Variety Performance in Louisiana

planting.note: Plant dormant container plants in winter to early spring in very acidic, well-drained soil; Delite ripens mid-to-late season and needs a second rabbiteye cultivar such as Tifblue or Climax nearby for cross-pollination and full berry size.

directions: Amend soil to pH 4.5-5.0 with peat or elemental sulfur well before planting; Delite is a USDA-ARS rabbiteye blueberry released from the small fruit research station at Poplarville, Mississippi, and prized among Gulf South gardeners for having the sweetest, lowest-acid flavor of the classic mid-century rabbiteye releases. Berries are medium-sized, dull blue, and ripen over a fairly long mid-to-late season window, making Delite a good choice for spreading out the fresh-eating harvest rather than a single heavy flush. Plants are vigorous and productive but need a compatible rabbiteye pollinator within about 50 feet, since Delite sets poorly on its own. Mulch heavily with pine bark or pine straw to protect the shallow, fibrous root system from Gulf Coast summer heat, and avoid phosphorus-heavy fertilizers that blueberries tolerate poorly.
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service — Small Fruit Research Station, Poplarville MS

planting.note: Plant during winter dormancy in very acidic, well-drained soil; Excel is an early-ripening University of Georgia rabbiteye release with a relatively low chill requirement that suits Gulf South winters. Plant with Climax or another early rabbiteye for cross-pollination.

directions: Amend soil to pH 4.5-5.0 with peat or sulfur several months before planting; Excel is an early-season rabbiteye blueberry from the University of Georgia breeding program, selected to open the harvest window ahead of standard mid-season varieties while still carrying good rabbiteye vigor and heat tolerance. Berries are medium to large, light blue, and firm, with a mild sweet-tart flavor typical of early rabbiteyes. Excel's relatively low chill requirement makes it reliable in zone 8-9 Gulf South winters that sometimes shortchange higher-chill northern varieties. It is not self-fruitful, so interplant with Climax or another early-blooming rabbiteye within about 50 feet for good fruit set and larger berries. Mulch with pine bark to keep roots cool and moist, and skip lime and phosphorus fertilizers, which blueberries handle poorly.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Rabbiteye Blueberry Cultivars

planting.note: Plant during winter dormancy in very acidic, well-drained soil; Alapaha is an early-season University of Georgia rabbiteye named for the Alapaha River in south Georgia, bred for good fruit set and leaf-spot tolerance in humid climates.

directions: Amend soil to pH 4.5-5.0 with peat or elemental sulfur before planting; Alapaha is an early-ripening rabbiteye blueberry released by the University of Georgia and named for the Alapaha River region of south Georgia, bred to combine early harvest timing with better-than-average tolerance of Septoria and other leaf-spot diseases common in humid Gulf South summers. Berries are medium-sized, light blue, and firm with good flavor for an early variety. Fruit set improves noticeably with a second rabbiteye cultivar planted nearby, since Alapaha is only partially self-fruitful. The upright, vigorous bush needs little training beyond removing old unproductive canes each winter. Mulch generously with pine bark or pine straw and avoid overhead irrigation late in the day to further reduce leaf-spot pressure in humid climates.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Rabbiteye Blueberry Cultivars
